story.what_it_does: ICICI Lombard is an Indian general (non-life) insurer selling Motor, Health, Fire and other commercial cover. In FY2026 it wrote gross premium of about ₹287 billion and earned profit after tax of ₹27.72 billion.
story.plans: Management aims to grow 100 to 200 basis points above the industry and keep Motor loss ratio in a 65-67% range. It also plans to scale up digital sourcing, hold expenses within 30%, and select commercial risks carefully rather than chase growth.
story.moat: The notes point to scale and a strong balance sheet: solvency of 2.74x against a 1.50x minimum, and Motor market share of 10.7%. Growth has lagged the industry, though, so the notes do not show a clear edge in pricing or distribution.

scenarios.story: Fire and commercial pricing pressure eases and the Motor third-party hit stays a one-off, so the combined ratio returns toward about 102-103%. Premium growth then catches up with the industry while the solvency cushion supports dividends.
signals_to_watch: Combined ratio excluding one-offs and catastrophe losses staying near 102.3-102.7%
Fire de-growth continuing to moderate from 32.1% in Q1 FY2027 and 21.2% in Q2

scenarios.story: Premium growth stays a bit below the industry (5.4% in H1 versus 8.9%) and the combined ratio stays a little above 100. Profit is helped by investment income and capital gains, with the Motor loss ratio inside its range.
signals_to_watch: Motor loss ratio staying within the 65-67% range
Premium growth versus industry growth (H1 FY2027: 5.4% versus 8.9%)

scenarios.story: The Supreme Court Motor third-party ruling adds more reserves, and health claims and commercial competition keep pushing claims up. Weak premium growth and investment losses would then squeeze profit further.
signals_to_watch: Motor third-party loss ratio rising 12% to 15% after the judgement
Group Health loss ratio (97.9% in Q2) and commercial lines loss ratio staying high
